episodes.170551: An organized west-to-east line of early morning thunderstorms tracked from east-central Illinois into central Indiana.  Strong upper level winds and ample vertical wind shear combined with adequate instability to produce severe winds generally parallel to, and north of Interstate 70.  Strongest winds were found where the wind shear was best oriented to the squall line's progression:  across the Indianapolis metro area and points east.  A gustnado in Anderson (Madison County) also caused minor damage.  The episode's strongest winds likely occurred in the evening when a more isolated thunderstorm impacted Rush County.
episodes.170560: Despite the high pressure centered more over western New Mexico, an abundant amount of moisture still resided within the atmosphere. This led to scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across much of the central and western New Mexico, some of which produced very heavy rainfall. Flash flooding and even a report of large hail was reported across portions of central New Mexico.
episodes.170686: Northwesterly mean low-level flow was accompanied by an unusually-cold air mass over Lake Erie during the morning of the 2nd. Despite marginal lake-induced instability, a couple of non-mesocyclonic waterspouts occurred. Radar and satellite data indicated these waterspouts accompanied a deeper lake-effect cumuliform cloud band that developed along a distinct low-level convergence and horizontal wind shear zone over the lake.
episodes.170723: Abundant monsoon moisture remained over the Four Corners region. Additionally, a shortwave disturbance moved overhead. This led to widespread showers and thunderstorms across western Colorado. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain. Some storms produced localized debris flows across the region.
episodes.170725: Plenty of residual monsoon moisture remained over southwest Colorado which resulted in another day of showers and thunderstorms across the region. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain. A localized debris flow occurred in Archuleta County.
episodes.170873: An isolated thunderstorm tracked across Loudoun County in northern Virginia causing localized wind damage during the mid evening hours.
episodes.170898: A couple of thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts over the upper tidal Potomac River and upper Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.170899: An isolated thunderstorm produced gusty winds over the middle Chesapeake Bay and tidal Choptank River.
episodes.171027: A warm front moved into Minnesota during the afternoon hours of the 2nd leading to the development of thunderstorms across the state. These storms were elevated in nature due to the warm front with large hail and heavy downpours being the primary threats. Some of the storms during the afternoon hours produced hail up to 2 inches in diameter across St. Louis and Itasca counties.
episodes.171135: Isolated thunderstorms produced gusty outflow winds across northern Nevada.
episodes.171301: Scattered thunderstorms developed in far southeast Wyoming near the Nebraska border during the afternoon of the 2nd. Storms produced strong outflow winds around 60 mph before quickly dissipating late in the afternoon.
episodes.171436: Small clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms moved southeast across the lower Wabash Valley during the late afternoon and evening hours. Large hail was reported with a couple of these storms. The storms initially formed along the residual outflow boundary left by an early morning thunderstorm complex. The atmosphere was very unstable during the late afternoon and early evening, when peak mixed-layer capes approached 4000 J/kg. Once the storms formed an organized cold pool, new thunderstorms developed on the western flank of the storm complex as an unstable southwest wind flow was lifted over the cold pool.
episodes.171437: A cluster of severe thunderstorms with widespread damaging winds affected the Evansville area. The storms initially formed over Illinois and west central Indiana along the residual outflow boundary left by an early morning thunderstorm complex. The atmosphere was very unstable during the late afternoon and early evening, when peak mixed-layer capes approached 4000 J/kg. Once the storms formed an organized cold pool, new thunderstorms developed on the western flank of the storm complex as an unstable southwest wind flow was lifted over the cold pool.
episodes.171439: Persistent clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms moved southeast across portions of western Kentucky. The storms first moved across the Ohio River into the Henderson and Owensboro areas early in the evening. The last of the severe storms exited the Pennyrile region of west Kentucky during the overnight hours. The storms initially formed over Illinois and Indiana along the residual outflow boundary left by an early morning thunderstorm complex. The atmosphere was very unstable during the late afternoon and early evening, when peak mixed-layer capes approached 4000 J/kg. Once the storms formed an organized cold pool, new thunderstorms developed on the western flank of the storm complex as an unstable southwest wind flow was lifted over the cold pool.
episodes.171454: Low pressure drew in a cold front beginning on the afternoon of August 1st. In advance of this feature, afternoon heating and residing unstable conditions contributed to the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms. Antecedent rainfall ahead of this event resulted in susceptible soil conditions, which coupled with heavy rainfall that day led to areas of flash flooding.||Mingo County was inundated with heavy rain on the morning of the 1st and continued to see rain occur into the early afternoon. The quick rise and continued deluge of water of the local creeks and streams resulted in flooding along the adjacent roadways. Residential bridges were washed out as a result of these heavy rains and also damage to several homes within the county.||The cold front arrived into West Virginia on the morning of August 2nd, which continued the threat for flash flooding across the eastern portions of the state. The boundary stalled nearby that afternoon, leading to several rounds of showers and strong thunderstorms. Braxton County observed a combination of strong winds and heavy rainfall, resulting in downed trees and flooded roadways.
episodes.171510: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over portions of Tripp County, producing some wind gusts around 70 mph.
episodes.171511: A thunderstorm that briefly became severe produced some wind gusts over 60 mph across western portions of Todd County.
episodes.171863: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters around Tampa Bay.
episodes.171864: Afternoon thunderstorms produce wind damage near Cypress Gardens in Polk County.
episodes.172099: A cluster of storms moved along the Interstate 90 corridor in central South Dakota during the afternoon before pivoting northeast into east central South Dakota during the evening. The system produced a number of reports of winds with an intensity around 60 mph, with a peak gust of 79 mph at Poinsett Colony.
episodes.172141: Weak southwest steering flow and high moisture resulted in locally heavy rainfall across NE FL where the sea breezes and boundaries merge in the afternoon and evening.
episodes.172375: Remnants of a mesoscale convective system created a few supercells in eastern Ohio that advanced into northern West Virginia/western Pennsylvania. Two tornadoes spun up from a single supercell. Despite meager instability, deep-layer wind shear was favorable at near 40 knots, and the storm tracked in a favorable direction to ingest rotating updrafts.
episodes.172387: To begin the month of August, a passing disturbance sent through a cold front on the afternoon of the 1st. Warm temperatures permeated overhead that day and helped to produce scattered showers and thunderstorms across southeast Ohio. Heavy downpours accompanied these storms, and with previous rain from days prior severely impacting soil conditions, the area was very susceptible to flash flooding. This resulted in one instance of a flooded road within Vinton County.
episodes.172527: Heavy rain fell over portions of north-central Saguache County producing flooding and closing down CO Hwy 114 for several hours.
episodes.172734: Heavy rain fell across parts of Highway 17 in Conejos County causing a mudslide and debris flow to block the roadway for a few hours.
episodes.172789: Strong and damaging winds occurred with outflow from a thunderstorm complex on the early morning of 8/3.  Most of the damage occurred in central portions of Upper Michigan.
episodes.172819: Localized flooding occurred in association with a thunderstorm complex over southeast Illinois and the lower Wabash Valley. Numerous showers and thunderstorms occurred on the leading edge of a southwest wind flow of warm and moist air. High pressure over the central Gulf coast states combined with low pressure over the upper Missouri Valley resulted in the southwest wind flow.
episodes.172820: Localized flooding occurred in association with a thunderstorm complex over southeast Illinois and the lower Wabash Valley. Numerous showers and thunderstorms occurred on the leading edge of a southwest wind flow of warm and moist air. High pressure over the central Gulf coast states combined with low pressure over the upper Missouri Valley resulted in the southwest wind flow.
episodes.172878: Minor flooding occurred on the Little Wabash River. An active pattern was in place as August began, fueled by above normal temperatures and ample humidity on generally southerly surface winds. Several rounds of thunderstorms from the 2nd to the 7th pushed the river above flood stage.
episodes.172921: Scattered strong summer storms resulted in gusty winds in excess of 34 knots across portions of the coastal waters.
episodes.172999: An outflow boundary from convection earlier in the day served as the primary focusing mechanism for numerous storm clusters along and south of I-70 from the late afternoon  of August 1st into the pre-dawn hours of August 2nd.  Some of the storms dropped very large hail up to 2 inches in diameter.  In addition, continuous back-building cells produced a swath of heavy rainfall in excess of 8 inches from eastern Effingham County across Jasper County into northeastern Richland County.  As a result, many roads were closed due to flash flooding.  The flooding lingered until around midday on August 2nd, particularly in the hardest hit locations from Dietrich in Effingham County to Newton in Jasper County.
episodes.173003: A persistent frontal boundary draped across central Illinois continued to be the focus for strong to severe thunderstorm development during the morning of August 2nd.  A low-level jet interacting with the boundary triggered the first cluster of storms across portions of Sangamon and Logan counties during the pre-dawn hours, with additional cells forming from Galesburg to near Lawrenceville as the morning progressed.  The storms gradually dissipated and shifted east of the region by early afternoon.  Scattered wind damage and flash flooding occurred.
episodes.173105: Thunderstorms developed across the state on August 1, with several producing damaging outflow winds across northern Utah and isolated flash flooding in central Utah.
episodes.173152: Scattered severe thunderstorms developed across north central Nebraska in the evening, bringing severe hail to the area.
episodes.173160: Scattered thunderstorms drifted erratically across southeast Arizona during the afternoon. One storm produced flash flooding near Huachuca City.
episodes.173186: Flooding was noted from heavy rains on the Cache River at Patterson in early August.
episodes.173189: Hot and humid conditions brought thunderstorms to the area with wind damage and large hail. Large hail was reported in Faulkner county and wind damage was reported in Yell county.
episodes.173243: Localized thunderstorm wind damage occurred in the Burley, Declo, Heyburn and Rupert  areas.
episodes.173244: A second day of thunderstorms brought more severe thunderstorms to southeast Idaho.
episodes.173252: Residual monsoon moisture and mostly sunny conditions in the morning allowed for a few thunderstorms to form over northern Arizona.
episodes.173316: A warm front moved across Minnesota and northwestern Wisconsin during the afternoon hours of the 2nd bringing a warm and moist airmass to the region. Thunderstorms developed during the evening hours ahead of a cold front pushing in from the west. These storms produced hail to around 1.5 inches in diameter and heavy rainfall leading to some minor ponding of water in spots. These storms also produced wind damage across Burnett, Sawyer, Washburn and Price counties as they moved to the east leaving trees and powerlines down in their wake.
episodes.173317: A warm front moved northward across western Lake Superior during the afternoon hours of the 2nd leading to the development of thunderstorms as it moved through. These storms were elevated in nature due to the warm front with large hail and heavy downpours being the primary threats. However, some of the stronger winds were able to mix down to the surface across the Apostle Islands with a measured gust to 59 mph being reported at Devils Island.
episodes.173418: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced damaging winds downing a large tree.
episodes.173467: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. One storm along the coast produced a measured severe wind gust.
episodes.173477: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts with impacts to trees and power lines along with heavy rain which resulted in localized flooding.
episodes.173556: A severe thunderstorm impacted areas of northwestern Minnesota, mainly Beltrami county, with large hail up to 1.25 inches.
episodes.173651: Isolated thunderstorms developed over western North Carolina throughout the afternoon. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.173652: Isolated thunderstorms developed over upstate South Carolina during the afternoon and evening. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Kings Mountain National Military Park.
episodes.173758: Surface-based thunderstorms developed across north-central Nebraska, and moved east-northeast along the Missouri River.  With up to 3000 J/kg of CAPE and deep-layer shear of 30 to 35 knots, spotty marginally large hail fell with stronger updrafts.
episodes.173789: Broad east to southeast flow advected in monsoon moisture, which fueled thunderstorms over southeast California. Several storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.173790: Broad east to southeast flow advected in monsoon moisture, which fueled thunderstorms over southern Nevada. Several storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.173869: Scattered thunderstorms developed across south-central South Dakota in the late afternoon of August 2nd in response to an eastward advancing short-wave aloft. Weak deep-layer shear and skinny CAPE profiles limited the overall severe threat, but a very dry sub-cloud layer allowed for stronger wind gusts aloft to reach the surface across portions of southeast South Dakota and southwest Minnesota during the evening hours. Observed wind gusts ranged from 60 to 80 mph with occasional reports of trees down and isolated structural damage.
episodes.173883: A remnant outflow boundary along the I-70 corridor was the focus for shower and thunderstorm development during the afternoon hours of August 2nd. A few of the storms produced damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.177584: Slow moving thunderstorms developed during the morning of August 2nd over central Mississippi and persisted for several hours. Widespread flooding occurred in and near the Canton area, where radar derived estimates indicated up to 8 inches of rain fell over a few hours.
